title: How Lost Was My Condition
description: How Lost Was My Condition in Tonic Solfa to AURELIA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 62, “The good Physician”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AURELIA; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: How lost was my con-di-tion Till Je-sus made me whole! There is but one Phy-si-cian Can cure a sin sick soul. Next door to death he found me, And snatched me from the grave, To tell to all a-round me, His won-drous pow'r to save.

lines: Next door to death he found me,
And snatched me from the grave,
To tell to all around me,
I thought a cure to gain;
Some said that nothing ailed me,
Some gave me up for lost;
And all my hopes were crossed.
First gave me sight to view him,
For sin my eyes had sealed;
Then bid me look unto him,
I looked, and I was healed.
Seen by the eye of faith;
At once from danger frees us,
And saves the soul from death:

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to AURELIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
